question: Why add MDCLXXXV A5 orbital negative-polar no-go verifier?

question: How is the R2 degree-5 moonshine datum certified as genuine without the full Monster character table?
answer: Two self-contained certificates from the three computed McKay-Thompson series (1A,2A,2B): (i) Norton n=2 replication - since 2A^2=2B^2=1A the degree-2 replicate is f^(2)=J, so C(1)+2f(4)=2f(3)+f(1)^2 and C(2)+2f(8)=2f(5)+2f(1)f(3)+f(2)^2 hold for all three (q^4 identity ties in the supplied degree-5 trace f(5)); genus-zero heart of moonshine. (ii) Degree-5 eigenspace integrality: dim V5^{g,+/-}=(dimV5 +/- Tr(g|V5))/2 are non-neg integers for 2A,2B; dim V5^{2A,+}=166638534360 = Baby-Monster-relevant fixed graded dim. Witness w33_moonshine_v5_replication_certificate.py, w33_paper.tex Prop 'The degree-5 moonshine datum is genuine'. Still open: full V5=sum m_i chi_i over 194 irreps. Commits 927da5bf,83015abf.

question: What fixes the holonet's logical-layer architecture (code + gate set)?
answer: Both are substrate-forced by W(3,3), not free design choices. CODE: the CV fault-tolerant encoding is a lattice GKP code (multimode GKP = symplectic lattice); the optimal lattices are A2 (1 mode, hexagonal), D4 (2 modes, densest 4-dim, strictly beats products), E8 (4 modes) [Conrad-Eisert 2022; Lin et al PRX Quantum 2023]. The holonet is 2 qutrits -> 2 modes (Sp(4,3) oscillator rep on L2(R2)) -> optimal lattice D4 = the substrate matter shell (W(D4)=192/triality/tomotope); A2 = q=3 hexagonal/SU(3); D4(+)D4 < E8 = R1 homology/gauge lattice. GATES: CV universality (Lloyd-Braunstein PRL 1999) = Gaussian (deg-2, Sp(4,R)) + one deg>=3 generator (cubic phase gate); the substrate's two lowest matter invariants are exactly deg-2 (symplectic form, Sp(4,3)) + deg-3 (E6 Cartan cubic on the 27 = the non-Gaussian magic). Degrees {2,3} = universal CV set. So A2<D4<E8 = QEC code tower = physics lattice tower, and {symplectic, cubic} = {Gaussian, magic}. Witnesses w33_gkp_lattice_architecture.py, w33_cv_universality_cubic.py; photonic_holonet.tex 2 new subsections. Residual = quantitative FT threshold. Commits 4bf469e8,497c0aa1,872bf1be.

question: How are the holonet's GKP code and gate set mutually coherent (not just separately substrate-derived)?
answer: They are welded by ONE group. The logical Clifford group of a GKP code on n qudits of dimension d is Sp(2n,Z/d). For the holonet (n=2 modes, d=3) this is Sp(4,Z/3)=Sp(4,3), order 51840 -- EXACTLY Aut(W(3,3)) = the 2-qutrit Clifford group mod Pauli = the photon-realized Clifford group ('symplectic closure=51840', already in the holonet paper). question: Why did the Pass 517 completeness test first report rank 0, and what was dropped?
answer: Two sampling failures, both caught by the checks rather than by inspection. question: Why is the factorial law now marked FALSE at q=3, after 14 passes of confirmation?
answer: Because at q=3 the law is decidable by exhaustion and it fails. The section space at q=3 has exactly 81 elements ((q^2-1)/2 = 4 inverse-closed pairs, q = 3 choices each), and the factorial law is stated as an equality for the MINIMUM over sections, so enumerating all 81 settles it. The exhaustive minima of v_lambda(tr D^m) for m = 2..12 are 4, 8, 8, 12, 12, 16, 16, 20, 20, 24, 24, whereas the law predicts 4, 8, 8, 10, 12, 14, 14, 20, 20, 22, 24: the true minimum EXCEEDS the stated value by 2 at m = 5, 7, 8, 11. All eleven exhaustive values fit v_lambda(tr D^m) = 2(m + [m odd]). Since 2*v_3(m!) = m - s_3(m) with s_3 the base-3 digit sum, the two expressions differ by s_3(m) + [m odd] - 2, which vanishes exactly when s_3(m) + [m odd] = 2 - a set that contains every m = 3^j. THE PRIME-POWER TOWER IS PRECISELY THE AGREEMENT LOCUS, which is why its four confirmed rungs 8, 20, 56, 164 could not detect this, and why every earlier test (at m=q, at m=p^j, or at |R|=27 and 81) was inside the agreement set. Scope is OPEN and no claim is made: at p=5 and p=7 the sampled minima match the law at every exponent tested, so whether q=3 is special (smallest possible section space) or the law needs revision for all q is unsettled. Unaffected: the Pass 519 transfer-matrix identity tr(D^m) = q*[T^m]_{0,0} and T = 0 mod lambda are exact regardless. Both papers now carry an Erratum and statements invoking the factorial law are marked conditional.

question: Why does Pass 519 say the whole trace is one entry of one matrix?
answer: Because the Pass 518 cocycle telescopes. Writing P_j = v_1 + ... + v_j for the partial sums, Omega = sum_{i<j} omega(v_i,v_j) = sum_j omega(P_{j-1}, v_j), so the weight of an m-tuple factorises along the walk it traces through R^2. Defining T on the q^2 partial-sum states by T[P+v, P] = d_v * zeta^{-omega(P,v)} for v != 0, we get tr(D^m) = q * [T^m]_{0,0} EXACTLY, for every m and every section - verified at p = 3, 5, 7 with the valuation gap equal to v_lambda(q) every time. Consequences: (a) every orbit result of Passes 510-518 is a statement about closed walks of length m based at 0, grouped by rotation of the base point, so the period-d classes are cycle types, the sieve is a Moebius inversion over them, and the closed form is the necklace count - the transfer matrix is the object all of them were describing; (b) every entry of T is a Z[zeta]-combination of the d_v with v_lambda(d_v) >= 1, so T = 0 mod lambda and v_lambda([T^m]_{0,0}) >= m with no work at all, which means the '+m' term of the factorial law is FREE and the law's entire remaining content is the excess E(m) = v_lambda([T^m]_{0,0}) - m. Pass 519 also refuted the factorial law at q=3 by exhaustion; see the companion decision.

question: Why did Pass 520 retract its own Newton-polygon explanation, and what replaced it?
answer: Because the profile it was built on does not exist. At q=3 the block D is 3x3 with tr D = 0, so the characteristic polynomial is x^3 + e_2 x - e_3 and the Newton polygon is fixed by (v(e_2), v(e_3)). A first draft asserted the minimising profile is (4,6), giving a single slope-2 segment, all three eigenvalues of valuation 2, and hence 'no factorial is possible'. Exhaustively over all 81 sections the profiles are (4,inf) x 32, (4,8) x 16, (6,inf) x 8 and (6,6) x 24 - NO SECTION HAS (4,6) - and the polygons are not uniformly single-slope, since (4,8) splits into a slope-4 segment and a slope-2 segment. The explanation was withdrawn before it reached a paper; it is the third merely-fitting story this programme has had to drop and the first caught in time. What survives is weaker and true: the eigenvalue valuations are constants (2, 3, 4, plus zero eigenvalues where det D = 0) with no dependence on m, so v_lambda(tr D^m) >= 2m and the exhaustive truth 2(m + [m odd]) is affine in m plus parity, whereas v_lambda(m!) is not affine - it grows like m - s_p(m). That is an observation about measured values, not a mechanism, and the parity correction of exactly 2 remains unexplained.

question: Why is the factorial law's failure probably NOT specific to q=3?
answer: Because q=5 shows the same signature. At q=5 the law is NOT attained at m=10 or m=14: the sampled minimum sits exactly 2 above it - the identical gap seen at q=3 - over 250 sections in the Pass 520 witness and 600 in a separate probe, while m=6, 8 and 12 do attain it. Sampling cannot refute the law, since the true minimum is at most what a sample exhibits and the q=5 section space has 5^12 = 244 million elements, so q=5 remains formally undecided. But Pass 519's suggestion that q=3 might be special - on the ground that its section space is the smallest possible, 81 elements - is withdrawn as the less likely of the two readings, and both papers were updated. The governing asymmetry that makes this hard: CONFIRMING the law at one (q,m) needs only a single attaining section plus the never-below check, which is cheap, whereas REFUTING it needs the entire section space, which exists only at q=3 since enumerability scales as q^{(q^2-1)/2}. Every confirmation recorded in the corpus is of the cheap kind. Related correction: I had proposed exhausting Z/9 on the ground that it has 9^4 = 6561 sections; in fact q=9 gives (q^2-1)/2 = 40 pairs and 9^40 sections, a 39-digit number.

question: Why is the q=3 even-m minimum now derived rather than fitted?
answer: Because the valuation profile turns out to be a complete invariant, and one profile has a forced spectrum. Across the entire 81-section space at q=3 the pair (v(e_2), v(e_3)) takes exactly four non-degenerate values - (4,inf) x 32, (4,8) x 16, (6,inf) x 8, (6,6) x 24 - and each one determines the whole sequence v(tr D^m); every section sharing a profile shares the vector. On the 32 sections with det D = 0 and v(e_2) = 4, we have e_1 = tr D = 0 by Pass 473 and e_3 = 0 by hypothesis, so the characteristic polynomial is x^3 + e_2 x = x(x^2 + e_2), whose roots are 0 and plus/minus mu with mu^2 = -e_2 and v(mu) = v(e_2)/2 = 2. Hence tr(D^m) = mu^m + (-mu)^m, which is 0 for odd m and 2 mu^m for even m, and since 2 is a unit at p=3, v_lambda(tr D^m) = 2m exactly. That is the exhaustive even-m minimum, proved, and it replaces the Newton-polygon explanation Pass 520 retracted. The parity term is the same fact from the other side: those minimising sections vanish IDENTICALLY at odd m rather than cancelling by one order, so odd m must be served by the other profiles, whose minimum is 2(m+1), attained by (6,6) at m=3,9 and by (4,8) at m=5,7. So '[m odd]' is a switch between which profile attains the minimum, not a correction applied to one formula. Why those profiles give 2(m+1) remains open. Pass 521, commit fba8e1c5b, 12/12 exact and idempotent.

question: What is the agreement-locus blind spot, and which corpus claims does it affect?
answer: A fitted law confirmed only at points where it agrees with the truth receives no evidence at all. The factorial law survived fourteen passes because every confirmation was at m=q, at m=p^j, or at |R|=27 and 81 - and m=q satisfies s_p(p) + [p odd] = 1 + 1 = 2 for EVERY prime, while m=p^j has s_p(m)=1, so both loci sit inside the set where the factorial law and the true q=3 law 2(m+[m odd]) coincide. The test set was chosen for computational convenience, since prime powers are exactly where the cyclic-orbit decomposition collapses to a single class, and that convenience selected precisely the locus where the two formulas cannot be distinguished. Affected claims: the factorial law itself (P505-P517), the '3q-1 at m=q' shadow (P505/P506), and the prime-power tower 8/20/56/164 (P512/P516) - all three confirm both formulas and distinguish neither. NOT affected: the sieve theorem and its corollaries (P511-P517), which are exact identities verified against honest enumeration rather than fits, and whose completeness test measured a rank rather than checking a prediction; and the determinant law (P479-P491), proved unconditionally for f>=2 and verified exhaustively at q=3. The lesson is mechanical and searchable: for every fitted law in the ledger, ask whether its test set was chosen independently of the fit.

question: Why was the sieve completeness claim of Passes 516-517 retracted?
answer: Because the blind-spot test proposed in Pass 521 fires on it. The sieve predicts |T| independent linear relations among the tau(m) cyclic classes, where T = {t | m : m/t odd, e | (m/t)}. Choosing cells with |T| = 0, where it predicts NONE, a spurious relation has nowhere to hide - and in all five such cells, (3,2), (3,4), (3,10), (5,4) and (5,6), the measured nullity is 1 rather than 0. The missing relation is identified, not merely measured: the period-one class consists of the constant m-tuples (v,...,v), whose zero-sum condition is m*v = 0 with v nonzero, which is solvable exactly when p divides m; so when p does not divide m the class is EMPTY and S_1 = 0 holds vacuously. The sieve counts relations forced by cancellation and does not count vacuous classes, so it undercounts by exactly one whenever p does not divide m. Corrected law: nullity = |T| + [p does not divide m], verified on eleven cells across both regimes. Crucially this is the SECOND instance in three passes of the agreement-locus failure mode: all ten cells used by Passes 516 and 517 satisfy p | m, so the correction term was zero in every one. They were not chosen adversarially - the Pass 514 shortcut requires e | (m/d), a condition on p dividing m, so the AFFORDABLE cells were exactly the cells where the claim cannot fail. Convenience and the blind spot were the same constraint. Directional note: a larger sample can only lower a measured rank and hence raise the nullity, so an excess relation found this way cannot be a sampling artefact in the direction that matters. Pass 522, commit f84442a5c, 6/6 exact and idempotent.

question: Why is Pass 517's free(m)=1 iff m is a power of p now retracted, and what is the transferable lesson?
answer: Because its input formula omitted the vacuous class. Pass 517 proved the characterisation from free(m) = tau(m) - |T|, and that formula undercounts: Pass 522 showed the true relation count is |T| + [p does not divide m], the extra relation being S_1 = 0 from the EMPTY period-one class. Pass 523 proved the census exactly - the period-d class is empty if and only if d = 1 and p does not divide m, since the zero-sum condition (m/d) sum w_i = 0 is automatic when p divides m/d, reads w = 0 at d = 1 otherwise (excluded), and is satisfiable by (w,-w) for d >= 2 because 2w is nonzero for odd p. So the corrected count is free(m) = tau(m) - |T| - [p does not divide m], under which any prime l distinct from p has tau = 2, |T| = 0 and correction 1, hence free = 1. Measured at (3,5), (3,7), (5,3), (5,7), (7,3): free = 1 in all five and none is a power of p. Corrected statement: free(m) = 1 for m a power of p AND for m a prime other than p. THE TRANSFERABLE LESSON: a proof inherits the blind spot of the formula it starts from. Pass 517's algebra was sound; its premise had been derived only on cells with p dividing m. This is the third firing of the agreement-locus test in three passes, and the first to propagate through a proof rather than a fit. Also in Pass 523 (commit 9e9646e93): the two relation families are complementary since |T| >= 1 exactly when p divides m, so their counts add without overlap; and the (6,6) profile is derived from Newton's recursion p_m = -e_2 p_{m-2} + e_3 p_{m-3}, closing the q=3 law entirely.

question: Why is the sieve completeness result a theorem rather than a measurement, cell by cell?
answer: Because both bounds are proved for each tested cell. The LOWER bound nullity >= |T| + [p does not divide m] is proved: the sieve relations are genuine (Pass 514), the vacuous relation from the empty period-one class is genuine (Pass 523), and since |T| >= 1 exactly when p divides m the two families never coexist, so their counts add without overlap. The UPPER bound comes from exhibiting explicit sections whose class vectors are linearly independent over Q(zeta_p) - and exhibiting independent vectors PROVES a rank lower bound rather than sampling one, because the independence is exact arithmetic in the cyclotomic field, not a numerical estimate. Rank r forces nullity <= tau(m) - r. Where the two bounds meet, the equality is a theorem about that cell; eight cells are verified this way. What remains open is the statement for all m simultaneously, which no finite computation can supply. Also in Pass 524: free(m) = 1 if and only if m is a power of p OR a prime different from p, with free(1) = 0, repairing Pass 517's single-branch claim; and a negative result - at q=5 the valuation profile is NOT a complete invariant (220 sections give 34 profiles carrying 52 distinct trace vectors), so the q=3 derivation was a small-q phenomenon and that method does not transfer.

question: Why does Pass 526 say the transfer matrix has a symmetry rather than just an identity?
answer: Because probing the OTHER entries of T^m turned Pass 519's computed identity into a covariance statement. For a in R^2 let S_a be the permutation P -> P + a of the partial-sum states and U_a the diagonal matrix with entries zeta^{omega(a,P)}. Then U_a T = S_a T S_a^{-1} U_a for every a - verified with ZERO failures over all q^2 translations at p = 3, 5, 7. Both sides send the basis vector at P to a multiple of the one at P+v, and the multipliers agree because omega is bilinear and alternating. Two exact corollaries follow: conjugation by S_a U_a carries the (0,0) entry of T^m to the (a,a) entry, so T^m has CONSTANT DIAGONAL; and summing that diagonal gives tr(T^m) = q^2 [T^m]_{0,0} = q tr(D^m). This explains the factor q in Pass 519's tr(D^m) = q [T^m]_{0,0}, which that pass left unexplained - it is the number of states in a translation orbit, not an accident of normalisation. Consequence for the open problem: the factorial law's residue E(m) = v_lambda([T^m]_{0,0}) - m is now a statement about tr(T^m), hence a SIMILARITY INVARIANT of T, so anything computing T's spectrum computes E(m) for all m at once - which the cyclic-orbit decomposition could never do because its classes are not similarity invariants. No spectrum is computed and this is a reformulation, not a derivation; Pass 520's Newton-polygon reformulation had to be retracted. Pass 526, commit 444c5163e.

question: What is the final localization of the Heisenberg-Weyl open problem, and what is the q=3 answer?
answer: Every framework in the arc collapsed to one object. tr(D^m) = q[T^m]_00 and charpoly(T) = charpoly(D)^q, so the transfer matrix carries exactly D's spectral information and nothing more - which deflates my own Pass 526 suggestion that computing T's spectrum would settle all m at once. The cyclic-orbit decomposition, the sieve and the closed form are re-expressions of the same power sums. And the trace-valuation vector is a FUNCTION of charpoly(D), verified on 160 distinct characteristic polynomials at q=5 with none mapping to two vectors. So the open problem is exactly: given charpoly(D), compute v_lambda(sum_j nu_j^m). At q=3 this is now completely answered: exhaustively over all 81 sections exactly SIX characteristic polynomials occur, all with rational integer coefficients - x^3, x^3-9x, x^3-18x, x^3-27x, x^3-27x-27, x^3-36x-81 - with multiplicities 1, 8, 24, 8, 24, 16. The entire q=3 law is therefore a six-row lookup table, the derivations of Passes 521-523 are its rows computed by hand, and the minimum over the six reproduces 2(m+[m odd]). The valuation profile of Pass 521 is the coarsening that merges x^3-9x with x^3-18x. This does NOT extrapolate: at q=5 the image is large (220 sampled sections give over a hundred distinct charpolys), so the finite table is a small-q accident of the same kind Pass 524 found for the profile invariant. Passes 527-528, commit 46aefee12.

question: Why was the q=3 charpoly integrality reclassified as reality, and what does that correct?
answer: Because the weaker statement Pass 530 left untested turned out to be the real content. Measured across 72 sections at p = 3, 5, 7: EVERY characteristic polynomial coefficient of D lies in the real subring Z[zeta_p]^+, i.e. is fixed by complex conjugation sigma_{-1}, without a single exception. The real subring of Q(zeta_p) has degree (p-1)/2 over Q, which equals 1 exactly at p = 3 - so at p = 3, Q(zeta_3)^+ = Q and REAL MEANS RATIONAL. The six integral polynomials found in Pass 529 are therefore not a q=3 fact about integrality but the general fact about reality, seen in the one case where the real subring is the rationals. Measured rational coefficients: 30/30 at p=3, 0/30 at p=5, 0/12 at p=7; real coefficients 72/72. THE CORRECTION: Pass 530 tested whether rational integrality generalises, found zero of 40 q=5 sections, and filed it as the fourth q=3 regularity in a week to fail, alongside the profile invariant (Pass 524) and the finiteness of the charpoly image (Pass 528). It also listed the real-subring statement as explicitly untested. That entry is now WITHDRAWN from the list - the literal statement fails but the phenomenon generalises perfectly. The other three entries stand. THE LESSON: when a generalisation fails, the next move is to weaken it, not to file it. Pass 530 named the weaker version and did not test it. Relation to prior work: Pass 491 proved and formalised that D Hermitian forces det D in Z[zeta_p]^+; this is the same statement for every elementary symmetric function, and the natural proof (D Hermitian implies a real charpoly) is stated but NOT carried out. Pass 531, commit eb01c1e4b, 4/4 exact and idempotent.

question: What did the symplectic group buy, and what is the q=5 image bounded by?
answer: Two results, Passes 536-537. FIRST: charpoly(D) is an Sp(2,p)-INVARIANT. The group acts on sections by (g.c)(v) = c(g^{-1} v), and the characteristic polynomial is constant on orbits - 0 changes in 180 trials at p = 3, 5, 7. Exhaustively at q=3, Sp(2,3) = SL(2,3) has order 24 and acts on the 81 sections with SEVEN orbits of sizes 1, 8, 8, 8, 8, 24, 24; six characteristic polynomials occur, so exactly ONE coincidence happens - two of the four size-8 orbits share a polynomial, giving the class of size 16. So the multiplicities 1, 8, 8, 16, 24, 24 that Pass 535 left unexplained are ORBIT SIZES with a single merge, not a numerical accident. SECOND: the orbit count in closed form. Sp(2,p) permutes the (q^2-1)/2 antipodal pairs with a sign; a cycle of net sign -1 forces c=0 there since 2c=0 with p odd, while a sign-positive cycle is free, so |Fix(g)| = p^(sign-positive cycles) and Burnside gives 7 orbits at p=3, 2,034,735 at p=5, and about 5.7e17 at p=7. The p=3 value agrees with the exhaustive computation, which validates the sign bookkeeping. Since charpoly is Sp-invariant, the image of the section space in charpoly space is a quotient of the ORBIT space, so the q=5 image is AT MOST 2,034,735 - a hard bound where Pass 528 had only a 220-section sample. Consequence for the frontier: whatever refines the valuation profile at q=5 (34 profiles carrying 52 trace vectors, Pass 524) must ITSELF be an Sp(2,5)-invariant. The q=3 merge is located at x^3-36x-81, the lattice point (a,b)=(4,3); why those two orbits merge is NOT explained. Also tried and failed: leading units mod lambda do not refine the profile (still 34). Commits f968549ca, 23d4ab1fb.

question: Why is the Pages deploy queue the real website blocker, and what unwedged it?
answer: Pass 4204 session: the site served bytes 116KB behind the repo for hours. Two causes. (1) Nine workflows fire on every push (ci, pytest, rediscovery-ratio, runtime-frontier-release-lock, and five per-pass ones); with two agents pushing reservation commits constantly and only 4 concurrent runners, the queue reached 109 with the Pages deploy at the back. (2) The deploy run itself wedged: queued 100 minutes even after the queue drained to 2. Fix: cancel the queued backlog via the REST API, cancel the wedged run, re-dispatch pages-deploy.yml. It then ran and check_site_is_current.py reports served bytes == local bytes exactly (1,867,984, 116 sections). Gotcha: gh api needs endpoints WITHOUT a leading slash under Git Bash, or MSYS rewrites them to C:/Program Files/Git/...

question: Why was the 3.23% Ramanujan shortfall withdrawn, and what was wrong in Pass 4204(c)?
answer: Pass 4213: the blueprint graded the instruction graph as 3.23% short of Ramanujan by comparing |lambda_2|=0.893992320 against 2*sqrt(3)/4 for a 4-regular graph. The measurement is exact and reproduces from the real ISA (doubly stochastic, uniform stationary, mixing 15 instructions), but the graph has degrees 2-8, and 2*sqrt(k-1)/k is a k-REGULAR bound because the universal cover of a k-regular graph is the k-regular tree. So the verdict is withdrawn and the blueprint now states a comparison, not a grade. Third instance of the same error on this object (3060, 4201, 3042), all traceable to the Cayley/Schreier misnomer fixed at 4203. ALSO: Pass 4204(c) was mine and wrong -- it profiled F_p+F_f+CX_pf+CX_fp as 'the ISA'. The real ISA (Pass 2866) is F_p+CX_pf+CX_fp+Z_p: three linear opcodes and ONE TRANSLATION. Lesson: read the source, do not recall it; and the tell was self-evident since Pass 4204(a) had just proved no Clifford-only set can be universal.

question: How was the instruction graph's Ihara zeta finally computed, after three withdrawn attempts?
answer: Passes 4222-4226: use the HASHIMOTO non-backtracking matrix, not Bass. zeta^-1(u)=det(I-uB) holds for ANY finite graph -- no vertex degree appears in the definition -- whereas Bass's determinant relation assumes a common degree, which is why Passes 3060, 4201 and 3042 were all withdrawn. The instruction graph has V=81, E=261, so B is only 522x522: the computation was available at Pass 3060. Result: rho(B)=5.746872680, and of 161 non-trivial Hashimoto eigenvalues NONE lies on |lambda|=sqrt(rho), so the instruction graph does NOT satisfy the graph Riemann Hypothesis. Validated first on K4 and on the parallel track's Pass 4191 Levi closed form, both reproduced exactly. Also: 1-WL refines the degree partition 5 -> 17 cells, so symmetry does not explain the irregularity; minimum load ports = 1 in any direction (proved by the orbit of e_i, size 80/80, not by enumerating 4.2M elements). Generalisable lesson: when a formula keeps failing on an object, check whether the object satisfies its HYPOTHESIS before improving the estimate.

question: Why do exactly the regular generating sets satisfy the graph RH, and what did the reference graphs catch?
answer: Passes 4227-4231. (a) Over all 258 connected generating sets of size 4-5, the sets satisfying the graph Riemann Hypothesis are EXACTLY the 3 regular sets -- all the same discrete torus C_3^4 (S_f/S_p draw no new edges), none universal. So RH <=> regular <=> abelian <=> cannot compute: the instruction layer cannot be spectrally extremal for the same reason it can compute. (b) A pipeline bug was caught only by running graphs with known answers: W(3,3) returned 78/79 poles on the circle, and since 78=dim(E6) is the repo's standing count, 78 was right and the DENOMINATOR was wrong -- the Perron root rho was being counted as non-trivial (and +-rho for the bipartite Levi graph). Fixed: 78/78 and 156/156, both RH TRUE; instruction graph 0/160, RH FALSE. LESSON: validating det(I-uB) against closed forms (Pass 4222) did NOT validate the RH classifier built on top of it -- calibrate each layer against a known answer, not just the bottom one. (c) scripts/test_checker_recall.py now plants fresh faults sharing no bytes with the originals; recall 1.0 on 6 families plus a clean-file false-positive check.

question: Why was the degree-3 minimal polynomial for rho(B) rejected, and how should PSLQ results be guarded?
answer: Pass 4236. PSLQ offered 15668303 x^3 - 4686695 x^2 - 824152814 x + 1917252871 for rho(B)=5.7468726799 with relative residual 4.8e-26 -- looked convincing. REJECTED on two independent grounds. (1) ALGEBRAIC: rho is an eigenvalue of an integer matrix, hence an algebraic integer, hence its minimal polynomial over Q is MONIC with integer coefficients; any PSLQ relation must therefore be an integer multiple of a monic polynomial, i.e. its leading coefficient must divide all others. 15668303 does not divide 1917252871, so rho cannot satisfy it regardless of residual. (2) NUMERICAL: the relative residual PLATEAUS at 8.33455e-37 across 60, 90 and 140 digits instead of falling -- a near-relation, not a relation. Root cause: PSLQ was given maxcoeff 10^12 on four terms with only ~25 trustworthy digits; you need roughly (deg+1)*log10(maxcoeff) digits. GENERAL RULE for this repo: when using PSLQ on a quantity known to be an algebraic integer, require the relation to be a monic multiple, and confirm by re-evaluating the residual at 2x precision -- it must FALL, not plateau.

question: What is rho(B) exactly, and where is the instruction machine actually slow?
answer: Passes 4237-4244. (1) rho(B)=5.7468726799... is an algebraic integer of degree EXACTLY 33 -- the degree-162 characteristic polynomial of the quadratic pencil, computed exactly over Z by interpolating 163 Bareiss determinants of 81x81 integer matrices, factors as degrees 1,2,2,2^2,14,14,16,16,20,20,20,33. Verified monic + irreducible + residual FALLS with precision (6.4e-32 at 30 digits -> 2.3e-54 at 60), the three guards that rejected Pass 4236's PSLQ candidate. (2) THE BOTTLENECK IS A FROZEN COORDINATE, not low degree. The slowest Hashimoto mode puts 61.3% of its weight on the hyperplane x2=0 while mean degree is identical (6.44) across all three x2 classes; weight/degree correlation only +0.14. Cause: of the 4 opcodes only CX_pf moves x2, and only when x0!=0 -- the other three including the load port leave x2 untouched, so x2 is nearly a constant of the motion. Prescription: an opcode moving x2 unconditionally, NOT a second load port. (3) Deflation of my own claim: the ISA's '12 of 360' rank is mostly a size effect; among the 24 minimum-size universal sets it places 8th. (4) log2 rho(B)=2.5228 bits/instruction of trajectory entropy vs Pass 2836's 8/3 bits erased per readout = a thermodynamic cadence of 1.06 instructions, WEAKER than Pass 2867's mixing bound of 15, so mixing binds first. (5) SIX workflow files could not be parsed by GitHub and failed on every trigger -- tell: GitHub lists unparseable runs by FILE PATH instead of the workflow name. Classes: unquoted scalar containing ': ', and ${{ }} inside a FLOW mapping.

question: Did Pass 4244's frozen-coordinate prescription work, and how does the ISA compare to a null model?
answer: Passes 4245-4252. (1) THE PRESCRIPTION FAILED. Pass 4244 said 'add S_f, which moves x2 unconditionally' -- S_f moves x2 on ZERO of 81 frames (row2=(0,0,1,0), it moves x3). The reasoning went from the coordinate's NAME to an opcode whose SUBSCRIPT matched. Worse: only F_f and CX_pf move x2 at all (54/81 each) and no pool opcode moves it on all 81, so the pool cannot unfreeze it. A CONTROL (add an ordinary translation) improved mixing as much as either targeted opcode -- always run the control before calling something a prescription. (2) The deficit is a CONSTANT: all 24 minimum-size universal sets have min stir exactly 2/3; no variation, so the correlation I went looking for was NaN. Four generators cannot fully stir four coordinates. (3) NULL MODEL, never built here before, and the most informative pass in the arc: against 120 random connected 4-generator Schreier graphs the ISA is 0th percentile in rho(B) (LOWEST growth of all 120) and 100th percentile in localisation (MOST localised). Everything earlier passes called a failure is the price of being a 4-generator Schreier graph at all; only the localisation is specific. GENERAL LESSON: measuring against an unattainable ideal (the regular case) made the object look defective by construction -- always build the comparison class the object actually belongs to. (4) The 4-opcode walk is doubly stochastic but NOT reversible (243 one-way pairs, infinite entropy production); closing under inverses gives exactly 0. Logical gate reversibility != thermodynamic reversibility.

question: What is the single asymmetry behind the instruction layer's spectral defects, and does the zeta identify W(3,3)?
answer: Passes 4277-4284. (1) THE UNDER-STIRRED PAIR IS THE f-REGISTER. The symplectic form splits the register into orthogonal hyperbolic pairs p=(x0,x1) and f=(x2,x3); ISA stir is 1.000/0.889/0.667/0.667 so the under-stirred pair is exactly f. The opcode list says why: F_p, CX_pf, CX_fp, Z_p -- a Fourier on p, two couplers, a translation of p. THE ISA IS p-BIASED, and the slow-mode hyperplane (4244), tied pair (4250) and 100th-percentile localisation (4251) are one asymmetry measured four ways. (2) But symmetrising is HALF a cure: against a size-matched control it wins decisively on min stir (0.889 vs 0.667) yet TIES on localisation and is WORSE on mixing and growth. p-bias is real and is not what governs mixing. (3) ALL 28 SPENCE SRG(40,12,2,4) GRAPHS give identical zetas: rho(B)=11, 78 poles on the circle, all Ramanujan, all satisfy graph RH. So 78=dim(E6) is a property of the PARAMETER SET, not of W(3,3) -- a regular graph's Ihara zeta is determined by its spectrum and an SRG's spectrum by its parameters. What distinguishes W(3,3) among the 28 is its AUTOMORPHISM GROUP, which the zeta never sees. Any passage reading the 78 as evidence for W(3,3) specifically is over-reading. (4) Reversible closure costs 1.95x cells (103->201, yosys), RTL generated from the opcode matrices and verified by iverilog against Python on a 40-instruction program. (5) 2/3 is forced: affine fixed-sets have size 3^k so moved-counts are 81-3^k, quantised.

question: What are the two SRG(40,12,2,4) graphs with |Aut|=51840, and where did the 114 orphans go?
answer: Passes 4294-4298. (1) THE FINAL PAIR IS THE GQ DUALITY. The two graphs sharing |Aut|=51,840 agree on EVERY cheap invariant (rank 3, vertex-transitive, 160 triangles, 40 four-cliques, identical local spectra, both locally 4K3) and an exhaustive search confirms they are genuinely NON-isomorphic. Building GQ(3,3) from the symplectic form settles it: graph 27 = POINT graph, graph 26 = LINE graph, verified by explicit isomorphism. GQ(3,3) has 40 points AND 40 totally isotropic lines; for odd q the duality W(3,q)<->Q(4,q) is not an isomorphism. So they are two halves of ONE geometry separated by ROLE, not by any count -- and that is the same p/f distinction the register is built on (Pass 4282's p-bias). Identification ladder: zeta resolves 1 class of 28, |Aut| resolves 20, the last two are point vs line. (2) METHOD: comparing the NUMBER of distinct local spectra (1 for both) instead of the spectra themselves is the counts-vs-characters mistake; and when many independent invariants agree, test whether the objects are the SAME before concluding the invariants are weak. (3) ORPHANS 114 -> 6. Routing generalised to all three manuscripts (58 blueprint / 41 w33_paper / 9 photonic); placement made STICKY because re-guessing already-placed inserts on a vocabulary count churns manuscripts. 6 match no manuscript and are reported by name. question: Where does the ISA's p-bias actually come from, and are the 40 points and 40 lines the same G-set?
answer: Passes 4299-4306.
